scene_description: A pale bedroom with a low bed in the foreground, a large white cubby unit against the back wall, two floor lamps, a small bedside table, framed wall art, and a chair near the right foreground.

visible_objects.observations: Both images contain the main bed, shelving, two lamps, small table, wall art, chair, rug, tiled floor, and dark right-side panel. A white foreground surface visible at the lower left in the reference is absent from the candidate.
visible_objects.image_evidence: Reference and candidate, whole frame; reference lower-left [0.00, 0.80, 0.14, 1.00].

spatial_relations_and_orientation.observations: The broad arrangement is retained: bed left/front, shelves centered on the rear wall, art and table to their left, and chair and dark panel to the right. The candidate bed appears more horizontal and fully within frame, while the reference bed and shelf are viewed more obliquely. The candidate table is more exposed behind the headboard.

proportions_and_occlusion.observations: The bed and shelf occupy substantially more of the reference frame. The reference mattress masks the lower left of the shelf, while a gap remains between them in the candidate. The reference chair is much larger and cropped at the bottom; the candidate chair is narrower and also cropped. The reference right lamp is partly occluded by the chair, unlike the fully visible candidate stand and base.

materials_and_texture.observations: The reference mattress has pronounced quilted side texture and a subtly uneven top; the candidate is smooth and rounded. The reference bedside table has a glossy, diagonally streaked wood surface, while the candidate top has closely spaced straight slats. Reference walls look mint green and the bed frame is stronger purple; the candidate palette is muted gray-green and pale pink.

visible_geometry.observations: Both shelves are open grids, but the candidate has a denser, more regular grid with conspicuous dark joints, while the reference has wider cubbies and thicker-looking white partitions. The candidate mattress is a simple rounded block rather than the reference's textured layered form. Both beds have raised slatted headboards, though their apparent orientations differ.

camera_and_composition.observations: The reference uses a closer, more oblique elevated viewpoint, with strong perspective and extensive cropping of foreground furniture. The candidate is more frontal, centered and distant, exposing more floor and the complete lower edge of the shelf. The right-side dark feature appears wider and more cropped in the reference.
camera_and_composition.image_evidence: Whole-frame comparison; reference dark right edge [0.86, 0.17, 1.00, 1.00], candidate dark panel [0.88, 0.24, 1.00, 0.87].

lighting_and_shadows.observations: The reference has bright warm lamp pools on the walls, strong highlights, and a conspicuous angular bright patch across the floor and rug. The candidate is softly and more evenly lit, without comparable wall light pools or sharp floor illumination.
lighting_and_shadows.image_evidence: Reference walls [0.00, 0.00, 0.25, 0.46] and [0.74, 0.00, 1.00, 0.67], floor [0.51, 0.56, 0.90, 0.87]; corresponding candidate areas.

objects_regions.observation: Large oblique purple-framed bed with quilted mattress; candidate bed is smaller, horizontal in frame, and smooth.
Large white grid partly hidden by bed; candidate grid is smaller, denser and has visible dark intersections.
Reference right lamp has a broad shade and is partly hidden by chair; candidate lamp is smaller, with its base visible. Reference lamps produce pronounced wall illumination.
Glossy diagonal wood grain differs from the candidate's straight striped or slatted top.
Gray curved chair is larger in the reference and overlaps the right lamp; candidate is smaller and separated from the lamp.
Both show a pale framed abstract picture, but the candidate's marks and composition are simplified and the frame is smaller.
A cropped white surface and dark support are visible in the reference but not the candidate; viewpoint and framing may contribute.

most_important_visible_defects: Different camera framing and perspective change the relative size and overlap of the principal objects.
Shelf grid proportions and visible joints differ, and the bed no longer occludes its lower portion.
Mattress and table surface textures are simplified or different.
Warm localized lighting and the strong angular floor highlight are missing.
uncertainty: Only visible RGB projections are evaluated. Hidden surfaces, exact object dimensions, true contact, symmetry, and whether apparent placement differences arise from camera or geometry cannot be established reliably.
limitations: This is an automated visual comparison of two single images, not a human rating or a measurement of the underlying 3D scenes. Regions are approximate normalized image coordinates.
